games.blurb: Lure a flock of starlings through a string of gates before night falls. Startle them for speed, but panic spreads from bird to bird.
games.goal: Fly 15 birds through each of the 5 gates, in order and close together, before night falls (60 seconds of light) and before the flock drops below 15 birds.
games.howToPlay: The flock steers itself: birds stay close to their neighbors and match their heading. {Hold} anywhere and calm birds fly toward your {finger}; keep holding and move it to lead them. The lure pulls hardest on birds near it, but birds that get too close are spooked. {Tap} to startle the birds near the {tap}: they panic (turning red) and burst away from it. Scared birds still match their neighbors' heading, so a {tap} just behind the flock sends it surging forward, the fastest way across open sky. A gate only counts birds that flew through it in the last few seconds, so bring the flock through together. The sky darkens as the light runs out (the time left is in the bottom bar); if the flock hasn't cleared all 5 gates by nightfall, the round is lost. Fear spreads to neighbors and fades over time. Scared birds ignore your lure, birds packed too tightly get scared on their own, and panicked birds can fly off the edge of the sky and be lost, so be careful startling near the edges.

games.blurb: Draw scent trails to lead your ants to food over six days. The colony carries over, and every day brings something new: scattered food, storms, a second spider, a rival colony.
games.goal: Survive a six-day run. Each day, carry the day's crumbs into the nest before sundown (60 seconds on day 1, then 90) without the colony dropping below 8 ants. Ants alive at sundown start the next day.
games.howToPlay: Ants wander until they smell something. Drag to draw a scent trail (it uses up the scent meter, which refills). Ants follow trails away from the nest, grab a crumb, and walk straight home, laying scent as they go, so busy routes grow into bright highways. Scent fades over time. Spiders follow scent too, and move fastest on the strongest trails. {Press} and hold to make it rain: rain washes scent away, so you can throw a spider off a trail, but your ants lose that trail as well. Soldiers keep spiders away from the nest, and a new ant hatches for every 10 crumbs. Day 1 is a short warm-up with one pile and no spider. Every day after it has a new food layout and a twist: day 4 brings storm clouds that wash trails as they drift by, day 5 a second spider, day 6 a rival colony of red ants that raids the same food and follows your trails. Ants you lose stay lost, but overnight one ant hatches for every 10 seconds of daylight you had left, plus 3 more if you met the day's bonus challenge (bottom left). Lose a day and you can retry it with the ants you had at dawn, or start a new run. The ▶▶ button (bottom right) runs the day at 2× or 3× speed.

games.howToPlay: Fire spreads from patch to patch of grass, fastest downwind and on tall grass, and it can't cross bare ground. Drag to cut a firebreak: it clears a one-patch-wide strip of grass along your stroke but costs stamina (more in tall grass), which refills slowly. Draw over a line again to widen it. {Tap} to light a backburn: it's free and wide, and it burns up the grass before the main fire gets there, but it's real fire and it spreads like the rest. Burning out right against a cut line is the safe way to do it. The arrow in the corner shows the wind. It shifts every 20 seconds or so, and the next direction flashes 4 seconds before it turns. Watch for sparks: the leading edge of the main fire throws embers several patches downwind, so thin lines can be jumped.

games.blurb: Heat an iron bar and hammer it into shape: heat decides where the metal goes.
games.goal: Hammer the bar until every segment matches the dashed outline. Three cracks, or running out of fuel with nothing left hot enough to work, ends the round.
games.howToPlay: {Hold} anywhere above or below the bar to heat the part under your {finger} ({slide} to move the heat); it burns fuel from the gauge at the top. Heat spreads along the bar and always fades, and thin metal heats and cools faster. {Tap} to strike a segment once a small hammer mark shows above it. Temperature shows as colour: black iron is too cold to move (the hammer just bounces off), and striking dull red (no hammer mark yet) cracks the bar; from bright cherry through orange and yellow each blow thins the segment, hotter blows thin it more; white-hot metal burns away. The metal you knock out of a segment flows into its neighbours, mostly into the hotter one: a cold neighbour takes almost nothing. So to thicken a segment, get it hotter than the segment on the other side and strike the segment next to it. Arrows under a hot segment show where its metal will go if you strike it now. A green dot under a segment means it matches the outline. The legend at the bottom shows the working range. There is no clock: take your time, but fuel spent on metal that cools off is wasted.

mechanics.name: heat
mechanics.description: {Hold} to heat the bar under your {finger}, drawing from a limited fuel gauge. Heat spreads along the bar and radiates away; thin metal heats and cools faster; white-hot metal burns away.

mechanics.name: strike
mechanics.description: {Tap} to hammer a segment. Too cold and it cracks; in the working range it thins, more the hotter it is, and the metal flows into its neighbours in proportion to how hot they are.

games.sharedState: Temperature and thickness per bar segment. Heating writes temperature (faster where the bar is thin) and burning removes thickness; striking reads the struck segment's temperature (crack or how much it thins) and its neighbours' temperatures (where the metal goes), and writes thickness.

games.title: Island Census
games.blurb: Keep rabbits and foxes in balance on a small island for two years, one season at a time.
games.goal: Get through 8 seasons (two years) with both rabbits and foxes alive. Every season that ends with either species outside its band on the census meters is a strike; three strikes, or either species dying out, ends the round.
games.howToPlay: The island is a set of meadows joined by paths. Each season you get 2 moves, then {press} Next season to watch it play out. {Tap} a meadow to release 8 rabbits there. Drag across a path to put up a fence: foxes can't cross it, but rabbits slip under it. You can have 3 fences up at once, and dragging across a fence takes it down for free. Rabbits eat grass (meadows turn brown when grazed bare), breed fastest in spring and not at all in winter, and move away from foxes and crowding. Foxes eat rabbits, raise cubs when well fed, starve when not, and follow the rabbits: the orange arrows on the paths show where they're heading next. Numbers under each meadow are its rabbits (white) and foxes (orange). The meters at the top show both totals against their green band. Protect rabbits too well and the foxes starve; leave the foxes free and they eat the island bare. The second year brings one surprise, announced a season ahead.

mechanics.description: {Tap} a meadow to release 8 rabbits into it. Uses one of the season's 2 moves.

Each season rabbits eat grass and breed, foxes eat the rabbits in their meadow and breed or starve, rabbits move away from foxes and toward grass, and foxes move toward rabbits, except across a fence. The census reads the island's totals.

games.title: Loom
games.blurb: Stretch a knotted net onto a dotted silhouette and pin it there before the pins pop or the strands snap.
games.goal: Hold seven shapes in a row: cover every dot with a knot at once and keep it there for a second. Three slips (a pin popping loose or a strand snapping) lose the shape (one frayed strand snapping loses it at once), and snapped strands stay snapped for the rest of the run.
games.howToPlay: Drag a knot to pull the net: the knot follows your {finger}, and the further your {finger} leads it, the harder you pull. {Tap} a knot to pin it where it is (up to 4 pins); {tap} a pin to take it out, or drag it to pull it out and move that knot. A knot you let go of without a pin slides back as the net relaxes, so pin it quickly. Strands turn from linen to gold to red as they stretch; a red strand that stays red snaps. The ring around a pin fills with the load it holds, and a red ring shakes and then pops the pin. While you pull, the same ring around your knot shows the load a pin would hold if you pinned it there. A dot only needs a knot somewhere inside its circle, so the near edge needs less stretch than the middle. A taut edge between two pins lines up the knots along it, which can cover extra dots without extra pins. Later shapes add twists: a blue dot only counts under the blue knot, and dashed frayed strands tear at a third of the usual stretch, so keep them slack. Shapes are mirrored at random each run.

mechanics.name: pull
mechanics.description: Drag a knot to stretch the net. The pull grows with how far your {finger} leads the knot, and it raises the tension in the strands around it.

mechanics.name: pin
mechanics.description: {Tap} a knot to pin it in place (up to 4 at once); {tap} a pin to take it out. A pin holds its knot until the strands around it pull harder than it can hold, then it pops loose.

games.sharedState: Tension in every strand of the net (its stretch). Pulling writes it around the dragged knot; pins fix knots so tension builds between them, and each pin reads the tension of its strands (too much and it pops, releasing its knot and passing the load on). A strand past its limit snaps for good. Where the knots end up, which the silhouette reads, is set by that tension balance.

games.title: Terrace Garden
games.blurb: Tilt a terraced hillside to slosh water where each plant wants it, and open the gates to let it down the slope.
games.goal: Make every plant bloom in a short warm-up and then three gardens in a row, before the spring's water runs out. Each plant needs its own depth of water. Water that spills off the bottom terrace, leaks away or is drunk never comes back.
games.howToPlay: {Tap} the spring's valve at the top to let water out, and {tap} a gate at the end of a terrace to open or close it: an open gate lets water down to the terrace below. Tilt to slosh all the water at once: toward the gates to send it down, away to hold it back, or to pile it up at one end. On a phone, tilt the phone (however you hold it when a garden starts counts as level), or {slide} the bar under the hillside if tilt is off (on a computer, drag the bar or use the keys). Each plant has a stake with a green band: it grows while the water over it is inside the band, and drinks as it grows. Too shallow and it waits, too deep and it bubbles. An open gate still keeps a shallow puddle behind it, which only a tilt will bring down. There's no clock: take your time. If the hillside goes still, an arrow or a pulsing gate shows a move that helps. Spring water left over when a garden blooms carries on to the next one.

games.title: Bubble Glass

changes.text: 21 boxes in three chapters: Sand, Wet and dry (wet sand, dust, grates) and Two bubbles (touching bubbles join). The score is your time over a whole chapter, played in order. Levels 1, 4 and 5 reworked: 4 and 5 now reward melting.

games.blurb: Turn a sealed box of sand to float its air bubbles out through the vent. Sand falls, bubbles rise, and glass you melt from the sand holds it back. Three chapters, timed.
games.goal: Free the bubbles through the gold vent in twenty-one boxes, over three chapters. There's no clock on a box and no way to lose: if one gets hopelessly stuck, restart it. Your score is the time a whole chapter takes, played in order from its first box, restarts included.
games.howToPlay: Drag around the box to turn it (on a phone you can also switch Tilt on and turn the phone itself). Gravity turns with it: sand always falls and the bubble always rises, so one turn moves both, in opposite directions. Sand trickles past the bubble in open water, slower the deeper it is, but in a narrow tube the bubble fills, sand stops it: its outline turns red. From level 2, {hold} on sand to melt it into glass. The glass grows toward your {finger} while you {hold}, costs heat, and is solid: it falls as one piece and blocks sand and the bubble, so it can make a lid, a roof or a plug. From level 3, {tap} glass to shatter it back into sand where it is. That's free, but the sand falls wherever gravity says. If that sand would bury a bubble, or the glass is a lid, the first {tap} only warns: {tap} again to break it. Some levels point at where to melt from the start. Chapter 2 brings dark wet sand (heavy: a thin layer stops the bubble, it falls slowly and won't melt), pale dust (light and fast) and grey grates that sand falls through but the bubble can't. Chapter 3 has two bubbles: both must get out, and bubbles that touch join into one that is too big for narrow tubes. If nothing moves for a few seconds, a hint shows a turn, a place to melt, glass to shatter, or Restart.
games.keyboard: ← → or A / D to turn the box

mechanics.description: {Tap} glass to break it back into loose sand where it is. Free, but the sand then falls with gravity, often onto the bubble.

games.sharedState: The grid of sand, glass and liquid inside the box. Turning moves the sand and the shards (and the bubble the other way), melting turns sand into glass, shattering turns glass back into sand, and the bubble's path reads all of it: sand slows it, deep sand or glass stops it.

games.title: Tidewright
games.blurb: Flick sand onto a seawall and work the sluice gates to keep the village dry, wave after wave.
games.goal: Keep the water behind the wall below the flood line for as many waves as you can. Every 6 waves a season is won and the wall carries over.
games.howToPlay: You look out from the village at your sand wall, with the sea behind it. The white line shows how high the next wave will reach; the timer says when. Flick (a quick {swipe}) anywhere above a column to throw sand onto it: a faster {swipe} throws more, and a sideways {swipe} spreads it that way. Sand comes from a pile that refills slowly. Water that gets over or through the wall pools at its foot and softens it, and sand thrown into standing water mostly washes away. {Tap} a gate handle to open that sluice: it drains the pooled water out while the sea is low, but lets the sea pour in when a wave comes or on a spring tide, when the blue sea line stands above the gates. Drain in the calm, shut before the crest, build on dry sand. From wave 3 the sea seeps through the wall; later waves bring rogue waves, rain, spring tides, double waves and storms.
games.keyboard: ← → pick a column, hold and release Space to throw sand (longer = more), 1-4 open or shut a gate

mechanics.name: shore up
mechanics.description: Flick above a column to throw sand onto the wall there; {swipe} speed sets how much, sideways {swipes} spread it. Sand thrown into standing water mostly washes away.

mechanics.name: sluice
mechanics.description: {Tap} a gate handle to open or shut it. Open gates drain the water behind the wall down to the sill, or let the sea in when it stands higher.

games.sharedState: Wall height and standing water per column. Flicks raise the wall, and read the water (wet sand washes out). Gates lower the water, and read the wall's sea side (the sea pours in whenever it stands above the sill). Waves overtop wherever the crest beats the wall and add water; standing water softens the wall each second.
